<person1> Lost. That is a scary word, yes?

<person1> Good. So. At the end of the story, Leo finds his way home. But let us go back. Back to before that. Back to the start. 

<person2> Okay. 

<person1> Leo and Alice were friends. Good friends. But one day they had a fight. A big one. Leo said Alice took his key. His little gold key. Alice said no. She said she did not take it. 

<person2> What was the key for? 

<person1> The key opened a small box. A box with good things inside. Leo loved that box more than anything. So he was more angry than ever before. He walked away fast. Too fast. 

<person2> Oh no. 

<person1> Yes. Leo walked and walked. He did not look where he went. He was too angry to look. The trees got bigger. The path got smaller. Then he stopped. He did not know where he was. He was lost. 

<person2> That is bad. 

<person1> Very bad. Now. Let us go even further back. Before the fight. Before the key was gone. Leo and Alice had a good day. They played by the river. Leo put his key down on a big rock. He forgot it there. 

<person2> Oh. So Alice did not take it? 

<person1> No. Alice did not take it. Leo left it there himself. But Leo did not know that yet. He was still lost in the big trees. More lost than a little bug in tall grass. 

<person2> What did he do? 

<person1> He sat down. He took a slow breath. He looked up. He saw the sun. The sun was going down on one side. He knew that side was west. His home was east. So he walked the other way. Away from the sun. 

<person2> Smart. 

<person1> Yes. And he looked for the river too. He knew the river was closer to home than the big trees. He listened. Water is louder than trees. He heard it. He walked to it. Step by step. 

<person2> Did he find home? 

<person1> He did. And when he got to the river, he saw something on the big rock. Something small and gold. His key. Right where he left it. Not with Alice. With the rock. 

<person2> Oh. 

<person1> He felt more bad than angry now. He picked up the key. He held it tight. He went home. He found Alice. He said sorry. Alice said sorry too. Because she had said mean words back. 

<person2> Did they make up?

<person2> I will try to remember that. 

<person1> Good. But try not to get lost. That is even better.
